\(\text{Define the two-sided Z-transform of a sequence } \{x(n)\}.\)
answer: \(\text{The two-sided Z-transform is defined as: } X(z) = \sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} x(n) z^{-n}\)

lq.q: a) Define the one-sided Z-transform of a sequence \(\{x(n)\}\) . State its Region of Convergence (ROC). b) Find the Z-transform and ROC for the following sequences: i) \(x(n) = \delta(n)\) (Unit sample) ii) \(x(n) = u(n)\) (Unit step) iii) \(x(n) = a^n u(n)\) (Right-sided exponential) iv) \(x(n) = n u(n)\) (Unit ramp) c) Using the definition, find the Z-transform of the finite duration sequence: \(x(n) = \{2, 4, 1, 3\}\) for \(n = 0, 1, 2, 3\) and zero otherwise.
answer: a) Definition: For a sequence \(\{x(n)\}\) defined for \(n \ge 0\) , the one-sided Z-transform is \(X(z) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} x(n) z^{-n}\) . The ROC is the set of all \(z\) in the complex plane for which this infinite sum converges.

b) Standard Transforms: i) \(Z\{\delta(n)\} = 1\) , ROC: Entire z-plane. ii) \(Z\{u(n)\} = \frac{z}{z-1}\) , ROC: \(|z| > 1\) . iii) \(Z\{a^n u(n)\} = \frac{z}{z-a}\) , ROC: \(|z| > |a|\) . iv) \(Z\{n u(n)\} = \frac{z}{(z-1)^2}\) , ROC: \(|z| > 1\) .

c) Given Sequence: \(x(0)=2, x(1)=4, x(2)=1, x(3)=3\) . \(X(z) = \sum_{n=0}^{3} x(n) z^{-n} = 2z^0 + 4z^{-1} + 1z^{-2} + 3z^{-3} = 2 + \frac{4}{z} + \frac{1}{z^2} + \frac{3}{z^3}\) . Since it's a finite sum, the ROC is the entire z-plane except \(z = 0\) .
